corpus_gaps: No provision in the frozen corpus governs the creation, extinction on the holder's death, or renunciation of a life interest or usufruct over land. Deed of Gift No. 515 of 1986 reserved life interests to Gamini and Vinitha, and Deed of Revocation No. 525 of 1991 gave one up; both steps rest on Roman-Dutch law, which section 36 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance imports where the Ordinance is silent. This is why question one is reserved.

Prevention of Frauds Ordinance section 2 lists sale, purchase, transfer, assignment and mortgage but does not name donation or gift, so the notarial form requirement for a deed of gift of land is not squarely stated in the corpus text.
The Partition Law is not in the corpus, so the conclusiveness of the final decree of 2 February 1985 in case No. 111/P as the root of Gamini Perera's title cannot be sourced from any provision.

The expression next of kin used in section 3(1)(d) of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act is not defined in section 25 of that Act, so the class has to be filled in from the general law of succession.

The corpus text of section 3(1)(d) of Act No. 38 of 2014 appears to be defective: it reads 'to a next of kin (who is a foreigner) of the in accordance with the applicable law of succession', with one or more words missing after 'of the'. The excerpt is reproduced as it stands in the corpus.

The corpus text of section 2 of the 2018 Amendment Act is truncated: the substituted paragraph (b) and the new paragraph (i) are not reproduced in the section body, so the amendment's content had to be read off the consolidated text of section 3 of the principal Act.

No provision in the corpus addresses the legitimacy or status of a child of a former marriage. Samantha is treated as a child of Suresh within section 24 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance on the face of the scenario.

Verifier addition: section 29 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, which disposes of the sibling portion where the only half-blood siblings are on one side, contains an exception where a grandfather, grandmother or higher ascendant related to the intestate on the other side is alive. questions.authority_requirement_reason: The intestacy limbs of the pedigree are pure statute: sections 21 to 27 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance decide every share taken on the deaths of Suresh, Rakitha and Muditha. Two earlier links in the chain are not. Nothing in the frozen corpus states that a life interest reserved in a deed of gift is extinguished by the death of its holder, and nothing states that a holder may renounce a life interest by notarial deed. Those are Roman-Dutch rules on donation and usufruct, which section 36 of the Ordinance itself imports where the Ordinance is silent, and they are needed before Suresh can be shown as unencumbered owner from 1991. A pedigree that omits them is incomplete, so the question cannot be answered from statute alone.

Whether Gamini's life interest ended on his death on 12 June 1990 and whether Vinitha's life interest ended on her Deed of Revocation of Life Interest No. 525 of 25 February 1991, so that Suresh held Lot A free of both burdens.
How Suresh Perera's ownership of Lot A devolved on his intestate death on 10 December 1995 among his widow Kanthi and his children Samantha, Rakitha and Muditha.
How Rakitha's share devolved on his death on 2 July 2022 leaving a widow Ann, and how Muditha's share devolved on her death on 5 June 2023 unmarried and issueless.

enrichment.original_background: Gamini Perera was allotted Lot A depicted in Partition Plan No 2525 dated 2nd February 1981 made by S Silva Licensed Surveyor bearing assessment No 20 Flower Road, Homagama containing in extent 10 perches by a final decree of a partition case bearing No 111/P dated 2nd February 1985 entered in the District Court of Homagama. Gamini Perera by Deed of Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10th March 1986 attested by R Liyanage Notary Public gifted said Lot A depicted in plan. no 2525 absolutely and irrevocably to his son Suresh Perera subject to life interest of Gamini Perera and his wife Vinitha. Gamini Perera died on 12th June 1990 due to heart failure. Vinitha revoked her life interest over said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 by Deed of revocation of life interest bearing No. 525 dated 25th February 1991 attested by S Sapumal Notary Public. Suresh Perera married Kanthi and had two children namely Rakitha and Muditha. Muditha died due to an accident on 5th June 2023 unmarried and issueless. Rakitha married Ann and died on 2nd July 2022. Suresh Perera died on 10th December 1995 intestate. Suresh Perera had an offspring named Samantha from his first marriage who is a citizen of USA (United States of America).

gold_answer_draft.issue: Trace the devolution of title to Lot A in Plan No. 2525, Assessment No. 20 Flower Road, Homagama, from Gamini Perera to the persons who own it today. Five links have to be established: the title Gamini took under the final partition decree of 2 February 1985; what passed to Suresh under Deed of Gift No. 515 of 1986; the ending of the two life interests in 1990 and 1991; the intestate devolution on Suresh's death on 10 December 1995; and the intestate devolutions on Rakitha's death on 2 July 2022 and Muditha's death on 5 June 2023.
gold_answer_draft.rule: Deeds affecting an interest in land must be notarially executed (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2). Inheritance on intestacy to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance whatever the domicile of the deceased or of the heirs (s.21), and Part III applies to the estate of anyone dying after the proclamation of the Ordinance (s.20). A surviving spouse inherits one-half (s.22). Subject to that half, inheritance runs first to descendants, then ascendants, then collaterals (s.23). Children take equally per capita and the issue of a deceased child take per stirpes (s.24). Where descendants fail and only one parent survives, the surviving parent takes half and the full-blood siblings, the issue of deceased full-blood siblings by representation, and the half-blood siblings related through the deceased parent take the other half (s.25). Where the only half-blood siblings are on one side, the full-blood siblings take one-half of that sibling portion first and share the balance with the half-blood siblings (s.27). Where the Ordinance is silent, Roman-Dutch law governs (s.36); the rules on the extinction of a life interest by the death of its holder and on renunciation of a life interest fall there and are not stated in any statute in this corpus.
gold_answer_draft.application: Gamini Perera held Lot A under the final decree in partition case No. 111/P of 2 February 1985. By notarial Deed of Gift No. 515 of 10 March 1986 he gifted Lot A absolutely and irrevocably to his son Suresh, reserving life interests to himself and to his wife Vinitha, so ownership passed to Suresh in 1986 subject to those two burdens. Gamini's life interest fell in on his death on 12 June 1990 and Vinitha's was given up by notarial Deed of Revocation of Life Interest No. 525 of 25 February 1991, leaving Suresh unencumbered owner of the whole from 1991. Suresh died intestate on 10 December 1995 leaving his widow Kanthi and three children, Samantha of his first marriage, Rakitha and Muditha. Kanthi took one-half under s.22 and the three children took the other half per capita under s.24, that is one-sixth each. Rakitha died on 2 July 2022 leaving his widow Ann and, on the face of the facts, no children. Ann took one-half of his one-sixth, that is one-twelfth, under s.22. Of the remaining one-twelfth, his surviving mother Kanthi took half, that is one twenty-fourth, and his siblings took the other one twenty-fourth under s.25; applying s.27, his full sister Muditha took three-quarters of that sibling portion and his half-sister Samantha one-quarter, that is one thirty-second to Muditha and one ninety-sixth to Samantha. Muditha then died on 5 June 2023 unmarried and issueless, holding one-sixth plus one thirty-second, which is nineteen ninety-sixths. Her surviving mother Kanthi took half of that under s.25, and the sibling half passed entirely to her half-sister Samantha because Rakitha had predeceased her without issue and Samantha is a half-blood sister related through the deceased parent Suresh.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The pedigree runs Gamini Perera, then Suresh Perera as donee under Deed of Gift No. 515 subject to two life interests that ended in 1990 and 1991, then on Suresh's intestacy Kanthi with one-half and Samantha, Rakitha and Muditha with one-sixth each, then through Rakitha's intestacy of 2022 and Muditha's intestacy of 2023 to the present owners Kanthi, Ann and Samantha holding 123/192, 16/192 and 53/192 respectively. The two life interest links rest on Roman-Dutch law and are not sourced from the corpus, so the pedigree is reserved rather than proposed as gold.

answer_claims.claim_text: Intestate succession to Lot A, being immovable property in Sri Lanka, is governed by Part III of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance regardless of the domicile of the deceased or the heirs.

The extinction of Gamini's life interest on his death and Vinitha's renunciation of hers by Deed of Revocation No. 525 cannot be sourced from any provision in this corpus; the Ordinance is silent and directs those questions to Roman-Dutch law.
On Suresh's intestate death on 10 December 1995 his widow Kanthi took one-half of Lot A and his three children Samantha, Rakitha and Muditha took one-sixth each.

On Rakitha's intestate death on 2 July 2022 his one-sixth split as one-twelfth to his widow Ann, one twenty-fourth to his surviving mother Kanthi, one thirty-second to his full sister Muditha and one ninety-sixth to his half-sister Samantha.
On Muditha's death on 5 June 2023 unmarried and issueless her nineteen ninety-sixths split equally between her surviving mother Kanthi and her half-sister Samantha.
The present owners of Lot A are Kanthi, Ann and Samantha, holding 123/192, 16/192 and 53/192 respectively, subject to confirmation of the two life interest links that lie outside the corpus.

questions.block_reason: A complete pedigree has to state why Suresh held Lot A free of both life interests from 1991. The corpus contains no provision on the creation, extinction or renunciation of a life interest or usufruct over land; section 36 of the Ordinance sends those questions to Roman-Dutch law, which is outside the frozen corpus. The intestacy arithmetic is statute-sourced and can be verified, but the question as asked is mixed_statute_and_case and is therefore reserved rather than proposed as gold.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: The question asks only for the fractions presently held by each heir. Every fraction is produced by sections 21 to 27 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance applied to three intestacies. The starting point, that Suresh Perera owned the whole of Lot A at his death, is given by the background: the deed of gift is stated to have been absolute and irrevocable, and the two life interests are stated to have ended before he died. A life interest burdens enjoyment, not the fraction of dominium an heir inherits, so the Roman-Dutch questions that reserve question one do not change any share here.

A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the intestate's property (s.22). Subject to that half, the right of inheritance runs to descendants first, then ascendants, then collaterals (s.23). Children take equally per capita and the issue of a deceased child take per stirpes (s.24). Where the descendants fail and only one parent survives, the surviving parent takes half and the other half goes to the full-blood brothers and sisters, the issue of deceased full-blood brothers and sisters by representation, and the half-blood brothers and sisters related to the intestate through the deceased parent (s.25). Where the only half-blood siblings are on one side, the full-blood siblings take one-half of that sibling portion in the first place and divide the balance with the half-blood siblings (s.27).
gold_answer_draft.application: Suresh Perera owned the whole of Lot A when he died intestate on 10 December 1995. Under s.22 his widow Kanthi took one-half. Under s.23 and s.24 the other half went to his children per capita. He had three children: Samantha of his first marriage, Rakitha and Muditha. Each took one-sixth. Rakitha died on 2 July 2022 leaving his widow Ann and no children on the facts stated. Ann took one-half of his one-sixth under s.22, that is one-twelfth. The remaining one-twelfth fell under s.25: his father Suresh had predeceased him and his mother Kanthi survived, so Kanthi took half of it, one twenty-fourth, and the sibling class took the other one twenty-fourth. That class was his full sister Muditha and his half-sister Samantha, who is related to him through the deceased parent Suresh and so is within s.25. Applying s.27, Muditha took one-half of the sibling portion first and then divided the balance with Samantha, giving Muditha three quarters of one twenty-fourth, that is one thirty-second, and Samantha one quarter of one twenty-fourth, that is one ninety-sixth. Muditha died on 5 June 2023 unmarried and issueless holding one-sixth plus one thirty-second, which is nineteen ninety-sixths. Under s.25 her surviving mother Kanthi took half, nineteen one hundred and ninety-seconds. The sibling half went to Samantha alone: Rakitha had predeceased Muditha and left no issue to take by representation, so under s.27 there was no full-blood sibling or issue of one to take the first half, and the only member of the class was the half-blood sister Samantha. Adding the three intestacies, Kanthi holds 96/192 plus 8/192 plus 19/192, Ann holds 16/192, and Samantha holds 32/192 plus 2/192 plus 19/192.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: As at April 2026 the shares in Lot A are Kanthi 123/192, which reduces to 41/64; Ann 16/192, which reduces to 1/12; and Samantha 53/192. Those three fractions total the whole. Two facts are open on the face of the scenario and would change the arithmetic if resolved differently: it is not stated in terms that Rakitha died without issue, and it is not stated that Kanthi is still living. The answer above assumes both, since no child of Rakitha and no death of Kanthi is mentioned.

answer_claims.claim_text: Intestate succession to Lot A is governed by Part III of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance because Lot A is immovable property situated in Sri Lanka, and the domicile of an heir such as Samantha is irrelevant to that.
A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the intestate's property and the balance passes to descendants before ascendants and collaterals.
Children take the descendants' share equally per capita, and the issue of a deceased child take by representation.

Where descendants fail and only one parent survives, the surviving parent takes half and the full-blood siblings together with half-blood siblings related through the deceased parent take the other half.
Where the only half-blood siblings are on one side, the full-blood siblings take one-half of the sibling portion first and divide the remaining half with the half-blood siblings.
On Suresh Perera's intestate death on 10 December 1995 Kanthi took one-half of Lot A and Samantha, Rakitha and Muditha took one-sixth each.
On Rakitha's death on 2 July 2022 his one-sixth passed as one-twelfth to Ann, one twenty-fourth to Kanthi, one thirty-second to Muditha and one ninety-sixth to Samantha.

On Muditha's death on 5 June 2023 unmarried and issueless her nineteen ninety-sixths passed half to Kanthi as surviving parent and half to Samantha as the only surviving member of the sibling class, Rakitha having died without issue.
Samantha is an heir of Suresh Perera even though she is a child of his first marriage, because children take equally per capita without distinction between marriages.
As at April 2026 Kanthi holds 123/192 of Lot A, being 41/64.
As at April 2026 Ann holds 16/192 of Lot A, being 1/12.
As at April 2026 Samantha holds 53/192 of Lot A.
The answer assumes Rakitha left no issue and that Kanthi is still living, neither of which is stated in terms; if either assumption fails the fractions change.

questions.block_reason: The verifier recomputed every fraction independently and reached the same result, Kanthi 123/192, Ann 16/192 and Samantha 53/192, so the arithmetic is not in doubt. The rule statement is. The decisive step in Muditha's 2023 intestacy is anchored on section 27, which on its terms gives the full brothers and sisters one-half of the sibling portion in the first place and so presupposes that a full sibling or the issue of one survived; none did. Section 29 is the provision for that case and has been added as PROV-M001-901. Section 29 also carries an exception where a grandparent or higher ascendant related to the intestate on the other side is alive, which the scenario does not address and which the gold answer does not consider. A lawyer must settle which section governs and whether that exception bites before this answer is used as gold; the verifier may not rewrite the gold prose, which still reasons on section 27 alone.

Whether Samantha can take on intestacy turns on the date of operation of the Act, on the terms of the section 2 prohibition, on the definitions of foreigner and transfer in section 25, and on the intestacy exemption in section 3(1)(d), read with the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance provisions that make her an heir. Every step is in the corpus and no judicial or common-law doctrine is needed to complete the answer.

legal_issues.issue: Whether the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014 reaches the devolution of Suresh Perera's estate, given that he died on 10 December 1995 and the Act is deemed to operate only from 1 January 2013.
Whether Samantha is a foreigner within section 25 of the Act, and whether a devolution by operation of law on intestacy is a transfer of title within section 2(1).

Whether the exemption in section 3(1)(d) for title transferred by intestacy to a next of kin who is a foreigner covers Samantha's entitlement, including her entitlement arising on the 2022 and 2023 deaths which fall inside the Act's operative period.
What the 2018 Amendment Act changed in section 3 and whether it affects the intestacy exemption.

questions.hop_count_basis: Four indispensable steps across two enactments: section 1(2) fixes the operative date and splits the 1995 devolution from the 2022 and 2023 devolutions; section 2(1)(a) supplies the prohibition; section 25 defines foreigner, which is the term the prohibition turns on; section 3(1)(d) is the exemption that disapplies section 2, and it can only be applied by going back to sections 24 and 25 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance to show that Samantha takes as next of kin under the Sri Lankan law of succession.

enrichment.original_background: Gamini Perera was allotted Lot A depicted in Partition Plan No 2525 dated 2nd February 1981 made by S Silva Licensed Surveyor bearing assessment No 20 Flower Road, Homagama containing in extent 10 perches by a final decree of a partition case bearing No 111/P dated 2nd February 1985 entered in the District Court of Homagama. Gamini Perera by Deed of Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10th March 1986 attested by R Liyanage Notary Public gifted said Lot A depicted in plan. no 2525 absolutely and irrevocably to his son Suresh Perera subject to life interest of Gamini Perera and his wife Vinitha. Gamini Perera died on 12th June 1990 due to heart failure. gold_answer_draft.issue: Whether Samantha, a citizen of the United States of America, can become entitled to the intestate estate of her father Suresh Perera, and to the further shares that came to her on the later intestacies, notwithstanding the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014 as amended by Act No. 21 of 2018.
gold_answer_draft.rule: The Act is deemed to have come into operation with effect from 1 January 2013 (s.1(2)), and the 2018 Amendment Act is deemed to have come into operation on 1 April 2018 (Amendment Act s.1). Section 2(1)(a) prohibits the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka to a foreigner, unless exempted under section 3. Foreigner means a person who is not a citizen of Sri Lanka, and transfer means any sale, donation, gift or any conveyance by or under which title passes to another person (s.25). Section 3(1)(d) exempts from section 2 any land the title of which is transferred by intestacy, gift or testamentary disposition to a next of kin who is a foreigner, in accordance with the applicable law of succession of Sri Lanka, and section 3(1)(e) separately exempts a transfer to a dual citizen. Alienation in contravention of the Act is void (s.18). Section 2 of the 2018 Amendment Act amends section 3(1) by substituting paragraph (b), altering paragraph (h) and adding a new paragraph (i); it leaves paragraph (d) untouched. Who is next of kin on an intestacy is settled by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, under which children take equally per capita (s.24) and, where descendants fail and one parent survives, half-blood siblings related through the deceased parent share in the sibling half (ss.25 and 27).
gold_answer_draft.application: Suresh Perera died intestate on 10 December 1995. The Act operates only from 1 January 2013, so it has no application at all to the vesting of Samantha's one-sixth in 1995; her entitlement from her father is outside the Act on temporal grounds alone. The shares that reached her on Rakitha's death on 2 July 2022 and Muditha's death on 5 June 2023 do fall within the operative period of both the principal Act and the 2018 Amendment. Assuming she holds no Sri Lankan citizenship, Samantha is a foreigner within s.25. Even so, s.2(1) bites only on a transfer of title, and transfer is defined as a sale, donation, gift or conveyance by which title passes, all of which are voluntary dispositions; a devolution by operation of law on an intestacy is not naturally any of them. More directly, s.3(1)(d) expressly exempts land whose title is transferred by intestacy to a next of kin who is a foreigner in accordance with the applicable law of succession of Sri Lanka. Samantha takes as a child of Suresh under s.24 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance and as a half-blood sister of Rakitha and Muditha under ss.25 and 27 of that Ordinance, so she is next of kin taking under Sri Lankan succession law in every instance. The 2018 Amendment does not disturb paragraph (d). Section 18 is therefore not engaged and nothing in her entitlement is void. If Samantha is in fact also a citizen of Sri Lanka, she is not a foreigner at all and s.3(1)(e) would apply independently; the scenario states only her United States citizenship and does not settle the point.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: Yes. Samantha can become entitled to the intestate estate of Suresh Perera. The Act cannot reach the 1995 devolution because it operates only from 1 January 2013, and the shares that came to her in 2022 and 2023 are within the express intestacy exemption in s.3(1)(d), which the 2018 Amendment left intact. Her entitlement is not an alienation in contravention of the Act and is not void under s.18. One caution should be recorded: s.3(4) provides that where a transfer is effected under s.3 the Act applies to every subsequent transfer of that land, so any later disposition by Samantha would be tested against s.2 in the ordinary way.

answer_claims.claim_text: The Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014 is deemed to have come into operation with effect from 1 January 2013.
Section 2(1)(a) prohibits the transfer of title of land situated in Sri Lanka to a foreigner unless the transfer is exempted under section 3.
A foreigner is a person who is not a citizen of Sri Lanka, and a transfer is a sale, donation, gift or conveyance by which title passes to another person.
Section 3(1)(d) exempts from section 2 any land the title of which is transferred by intestacy to a next of kin who is a foreigner in accordance with the applicable law of succession of Sri Lanka.

The 2018 Amendment Act came into operation on 1 April 2018 and amended section 3(1) by substituting paragraph (b), altering paragraph (h) and adding a new paragraph (i), leaving the intestacy exemption in paragraph (d) unchanged.
An alienation of land in contravention of the Act is void and has no effect in law.
Because Suresh Perera died on 10 December 1995, the Act does not reach the devolution of his estate at all.
The shares that reached Samantha on the deaths of Rakitha in 2022 and Muditha in 2023 fall inside the operative period of both the principal Act and the 2018 Amendment.

Samantha is a foreigner within section 25 if she holds no Sri Lankan citizenship; the scenario states only that she is a citizen of the United States of America, which does not by itself exclude Sri Lankan citizenship, and a dual citizen would in any event be exempt under section 3(1)(e).

Samantha takes as next of kin under the Sri Lankan law of succession, as a child of Suresh and as a half-blood sister of Rakitha and Muditha, so her entitlement falls squarely within the section 3(1)(d) exemption.
A devolution by operation of law on an intestacy is not obviously a sale, donation, gift or conveyance, so the section 2 prohibition arguably does not engage on its own terms.
Samantha can become entitled to the intestate estate of Suresh Perera and to the further shares that devolved on her in 2022 and 2023, and none of that entitlement is void under section 18.
Any later disposition of the land by Samantha would still be tested against section 2, because the Act applies to every subsequent transfer of land whose title passed under an exemption in section 3.
